Arms exercise

Tricep Dip

Dips lower and lift your bodyweight between two bars. Kept upright, they are one of the best compound exercises for the triceps, and with a forward lean they hit the lower chest hard.

By the FormFit Editorial Team · Reviewed October 2026

Primary
Arms
Also works
Chest, Front delts
Equipment
Parallel bars or dip station
Level
Intermediate

How to do it

  1. Grip the parallel bars and jump or step up to support yourself with straight arms, shoulders pushed down away from your ears.
  2. Keep your body fairly upright for triceps focus, legs straight or knees bent with ankles crossed.
  3. Lower yourself by bending your elbows, keeping them pointing back rather than flaring out.
  4. Descend until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor, or slightly above if your shoulders feel strained.
  5. Press back up by straightening your arms until your elbows are locked.
  6. Keep your shoulders down throughout; do not let them shrug up at the bottom.

Coaching cues

  • Shoulders down, chest proud
  • Elbows point back
  • Controlled depth
  • Lock out at the top
Advertisements

Common mistakes and fixes

Going far too deep

Stop when your upper arms are about parallel to the floor. Extra depth stresses the front of the shoulder.

Shoulders rolling forward and shrugging

Keep your chest up and depress your shoulder blades before each rep.

Flaring elbows wide

Keep them tracking back and close to your body.

Kicking the legs to get up

Use a band or assisted dip machine until you can do strict reps.

Sets and reps

GoalPrescription
Strength4 sets of 5-8 weighted reps, 2-3 minutes rest
Hypertrophy3 sets of 8-15 reps, 90 seconds rest
Beginner3 sets of 5-8 assisted or bench dips

Pick a starting weight with the one rep max calculator, and load the bar with the plate calculator.

Variations

  • Bench dip Hands on a bench behind you; easier, but limit depth to protect the shoulders.
  • Assisted dip machine A counterweight helps you build to bodyweight reps.
  • Weighted dip Add a dip belt once you can do 12 strict reps.
  • Chest dip Lean forward and flare the elbows slightly to shift work to the chest.

Muscles worked

All three heads of the triceps straighten the elbow, and dips let them work under your full bodyweight. The lower chest and front delts assist, more so the further you lean forward.

Benefits

Dips build pressing lockout strength that carries over to the bench press and overhead press. They need only a pair of bars and progress easily from assisted to weighted.

Safety and who should modify it

Dips place the shoulder in an extended position that some people do not tolerate. If you feel pain at the front of the shoulder, reduce depth or swap to close grip bench presses and cable pushdowns. Bench dips in particular should be kept shallow.

Frequently asked questions

Are bench dips safe?

In moderation and with limited depth, yes. Going very deep with your hands behind you puts a lot of strain on the front of the shoulder, so stop at about 90 degrees of elbow bend.

How do I make dips target triceps instead of chest?

Stay upright, keep your elbows close to your body and point them straight back.

How many dips should I be able to do?

Ten strict bodyweight dips is a good intermediate benchmark. After that, adding weight is more useful than chasing high reps.
